verdict.rationale: Dynadot's own security and transfer pages say it offers free domain privacy that hides name, email, and phone in public WHOIS, so the free, no-upsell part is documented. Nothing in the evidence shows privacy is enabled by default, and address redaction is not mentioned. Missing for 10: evidence privacy is on by default at registration, explicit address redaction, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, WHOIS privacy is free and on by default — my name, address, and email stay redacted without an upsell

citations.quote: Dynadot offers free domain privacy, account lock, two-factor authentication, and optional Registry Lock
Hide your name, email, and phone in public WHOIS
Enjoy free privacy, 1-year renewal, and 24/7 support.
